mia: Heads-up — we're seeing very low KV-cache reuse across short-lived sessions. Repro on prod-ish traces: only ~18% prefix reuse, memory growth after long contexts, and some fragmentation hits.
noah: Ack. Is this mostly due to key variance (session ids / per-request salts) or real token-prefix mismatch?
mia: Largely key design. We currently include full request-id + model+seq in the cache key. Any request with a new request-id becomes a miss even if prefix tokens identical. Also we discovered sticky routing isn't always honored for short-lived websockets, so same session can hit different workers and lose local cache.
perf-bot: Perf snapshot (2026-10-05T12:05Z): kv_cache_hits=0.18, avg_kv_mem_growth_per_long_ctx=1.1MB/request, kv_pages_evicted_per_min=4.2, prefix_fragmentation=0.27
noah: Oof. Two axes to try: 1) normalize cache keys to canonical prefix + model + quant/opt flags (drop request-id), 2) small prefetched prefix buckets for session affinity + lightweight sticky routing for websockets.
dmitri: I prototyped a hash-key approach last week. Instead of storing raw prefix bytes, we store a 64-bit fingerprint over the prefix tokens + model-version + quant-level. That reduces key size and collapses identical prefixes across different request ids. Quick psuedo: ```python
def kv_key(prefix_tokens, model):
    h = xxhash.x64(prefix_tokens.tobytes())
    return f:"k:{model}:{h.digest():016x}"
```
kat: Nice. Does the fingerprint risk collisions? How do we detect/handle false positives while keeping perf?
dmitri: Collisions are low with 64-bit XXHash for our workload (estimated <1e-9 per 100M keys). We still verify by comparing the prefix length + a short prefix-hash (e.g., first 128 bits of sha256) on mismatch fallback. That keeps common-path fast and rare-path safe.
mia: Also thinking of prefetch buckets — when session starts we can precompute and touch the first N prefix entries (N small) so the local worker populates cache pages and reduces page-in. This helps long-context chats where the prefix is reused across many messages.
noah: Agreed. Also tie this to batching heuristics: if we detect many requests with the same fingerprint in-flight, do an optimistic shared-batch to reuse KV across them. That reduces duplicate kernel loads and KV reads.
perf-bot: Local microbench (dev cluster): with fingerprint keys + 32-entry prefetch bucket: kv_cache_hits -> 0.63, p50 gen latency -8%, p95 -3%, memory overhead +2% (due to prefetch), page-faults down 48%.
dmitri: Caveat — prefetch increases short-lived memory pressure and can worsen eviction for multi-tenant workloads. We need spillback heuristics: only prefetch when session lifetime > X and QPS < Y.
kat: Can we add a quick experiment matrix? I can run combinations on canary: (A) key-normalize only, (B) key-normalize + fingerprint, (C) fingerprint + prefetch(32), (D) fingerprint + prefetch(32) + sticky routing. Track: kv_hit, p50/p95, evictions/min, avg_mem_growth_long_ctx.
mia: Yes. Proposed owners: kat runs experiment matrix on canary, dmitri wires fingerprinting in runtime (feature flag), noah toggles sticky routing logic in router layer. I'll collect traces and produce perf dashboard.
noah: One more: check kernel selection implications — if fingerprinting increases concurrent identical prefixes, that might favor fused-attn kernels vs memory-bound kernels. Add kernel selection tag to traces so we can correlate.
dmitri: Will add kernel tag and batch-id in logs.
kat: I'll schedule runs this afternoon. Expected results in ~6h. :eyes:
mia: Thanks. If the canary looks good we can roll feature-flag to dedicated clusters next. Also capture a short postmortem if we see any regression.
noah: Cool. For the JSON/metrics export use this CLI: ```bash
./tools/perf-harness run --suite kv-reuse --variants norm,fingerprint,prefetch --out /tmp/kv_reuse_$(date +%s).json
```
dmitri: I'll also add a small prober to check cross-worker sticky violations — emits `sticky_misroute` counter.
perf-bot: Scheduled: kat runs 4 experiments starting 1779005400; expected completion 1779020000.
kat: Got it. I'll post results in this thread when done.
noah: Thanks team. Small follow-ups: keep an eye on eviction spikes and multi-tenant regressions.
mia: End of thread for now.
